newsitem.title: UK: UK's Thatcher was deeply hostile to Germany - aide.
newsitem.headline: UK's Thatcher was deeply hostile to Germany - aide.

text.p: Former British prime minister Margaret Thatcher harboured bitter memories of World War Two and believed Germans could never be trusted, a diary to be published on Wednesday says.
George Urban, one of Thatcher's closest advisers, recalled that Thatcher was opposed to the reunification of East and West Germany, fearing it would give Germany too much power.

"The prime minister is extremely reluctant to see Germany assume a role other than that of a divided country, still controlled by post-war arrangements," he wrote in his diary after a policy meeting 1989.

"There are things that people of your generation and mine ought never forget. We've been through the war and we know perfectly well what the Germans are like and what dictators can do, and how national character doesn't basically change," Urban says Thatcher told him.
Extracts from Urban's diary were published in The Times newspaper on Tuesday.

Under pressure from her advisers, Thatcher reluctantly pledged to be "sweet to the Germans, sweet to (German Chancellor) Helmut Kohl," but added stubbornly, "I shall not be defeated. I will uphold my principles," says Urban.
Urban also says that Thatcher, who was known as the "Iron Lady" for her forceful leadership style, took just 22 days to lose faith in John Major, the man she favoured as her successor.
Urban met Thatcher three weeks after she was forced to resign in November 1990 and was astonished to hear her saying Major's government "had embarked on a policy of great danger."

"All the wrong people are rejoicing! That's a sure sign that they are walking down the wrong road," Thatcher told Urban, according to the diary entitled "Diplomacy and Disillusionment at the court of Margaret Thatcher".
Thatcher was forced to resign after 11 years in power and three general election victories following a revolt in the Conservative Party.
Political analysts believed she had been grooming Major for power but she became increasingly critical of him. She was especially unhappy about Major's improved relations with Europe, says Urban.
"It is the European involvement that is dragging Britain down...It is our participation in that unholy mess. Let no-one forget that," she is quoted as telling him in 1993.
